Before entering the single-line section between Bourne End and Marlow, you’ll need to prepare the route and obtain the line token. First, set the switches correctly for the Marlow branch. Then, collect the staff: this ensures that only one train can occupy the line at any given time.

Bourne End was once a through station, with the line continuing onward towards High Wycombe. Today, it remains a two-platform station, but its layout tells a different story. Only Platform 1 provides access to the Marlow branch, and due to its short length, services here are limited to just two-car trains. Beyond the station lies the charming single-line stretch to Marlow, affectionately known as the Marlow Donkey. The name dates back to the days of steam, when a small locomotive worked this quiet branch. The legacy lives on today, not just on the railway, but in the town itself, where the Marlow Donkey pub stands as a reminder of the line’s history.
